t: Section 4706(b) of the Atomic Energy Defense Act (50 U.S.C. 2746(b)) is amended by striking “$600,000” both places it appears and inserting “$1,000,000”.

fable.w: This section only raises a dollar threshold in the Atomic Energy Defense Act from $600,000 to $1,000,000. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely technical amendment to a statutory dollar amount. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It simply changes a funding limit or threshold within the existing law.
qwen_block.s: Section 4706(b) of the Atomic Energy Defense Act (50 U.S.C. 2746(b)) is amended by striking “$600,000” both places it appears and inserting “$1,000,000”.

opus.w: This section only replaces a dollar threshold ("$600,000" becomes "$1,000,000") in the Atomic Energy Defense Act. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, rulemaking, or right to sue. Any congressional notice in the underlying statute stays inside the federal government, so it would not count as participation either.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** The only tempting reading is that the underlying provision (50 U.S.C. 2746, on minor construction projects) may involve reports or notices to Congress. That fails for two reasons. Congress is inside the federal government. And this section only changes a dollar figure; it creates no process involving anyone outside the government.

There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or requirements to consult with states, tribes, or the public mentioned in this text.
